## PM check-in, 2026-10-29 18:4x slot (continued): the CI run this cycle's own earlier entry was waiting on came back red, for a real reason, fixed

NEXT FOR THE OPERATOR: watch the GitHub Actions run for commit 80f52eab5 (this fix) to confirm green; if `gate_tests` fails again for an unrelated reason, that is real work, not the exhausted-backlog state.

The 18:45 entry below handed off "watch run 40932546417 for green." It finished red: `gate_tests` actually completed end to end this time (6m10s in CI, `test_gate_keyword_demand_global_rescored_current.py` the one real failure out of 454 files), rather than hanging the way it usually does, so this is new signal, not the usual unchecked timeout. Read the job log directly via the GitHub API rather than trust the one-line summary.

**Root cause, found by reading the actual script, not just the gate:** `ops/keyword_demand_global.py`'s plain harvest path (`main()`, no `--rescore`) scores every query against the live `site/` corpus at harvest time, exactly like `--rescore` does, but never stamped `scored_against_commit` on the payload it writes; only the `--rescore`/`rescore()` path did. So every weekly scheduled harvest silently dropped the field the staleness gate depends on, and the file stayed in a permanent "never checked" WARN state until someone happened to run `--rescore` by hand afterward. `ops/keyword_demand.py`, the US sibling, has the identical bug in its own plain-harvest payload construction; it only wasn't failing today because its committed file still carried a `scored_against_commit` from a manual rescore after the last harvest, a coincidence of timing, not a difference in correctness.

**Fixed at the source, both files:** added `"scored_against_commit": head_commit()` (`kd.head_commit()` for the global file) to the payload dict each plain harvest already builds, mirroring what `rescore()` already does, since both paths score against the same corpus at the same moment. Re-ran `python ops/keyword_demand_global.py --rescore` (free, no network) once to stamp the already-committed file that was missing the field, rather than leave it broken until next week's scheduled harvest. Verified: `test_gate_keyword_demand_global_rescored_current.py` and its US sibling `test_gate_keyword_demand_rescored_current.py` both pass; `test_keyword_demand.py`, `test_gate_keyword_demand_global_not_stale.py`, `test_gate_goals_keyword_cluster_citation_current.py`, `test_gate_also_called_is_heading.py`, `test_room_also_called.py` all still pass, no regression. A full local `gate_tests` re-run (all 454 files) was started in the background to cover the rest of the suite before shipping further; its result, if anything new turned up, is recorded separately.

Checking what that kill actually left behind found the real story: the killed process's own grandchild, `test_audit_catalog.py`'s own `audit_catalog.py --include-fixtures` subprocess (pid 738), survived the kill as an orphan (reparented to pid 1) and kept running, because `kill -9` on the parent reaches only the parent, never a grandchild it spawned, exactly the failure mode `_run_bounded()`'s own 2026-09-30 docstring already names and guards against **when preflight's own internal timeout does the killing**. **Started a second, fresh `preflight.py` run and did not touch it this time.** Backgrounded, checked on periodically without killing anything, across roughly 100 minutes of wall time in this session's own current load (425 of 450 `ops/tests/test_*.py` files done by minute 70, all 450 by around minute 100). ## 2026-10-28, PM check-in (18:4x slot): red checks.yml found and fixed, root cause was a one-line stale citation, not a real defect

NEXT FOR THE OPERATOR: watch the next checks.yml run on this push (or fire one), because this entry's fix is the only thing standing between the current red run and a clean one, and confirming it go green clears gate_ci_conclusion_current for every cycle after it.

**Previous work finished, but checks.yml was quietly red since 18:11Z and nobody had looked.** Attached clean: the unshallow fetch ran long, so this entry waited for it rather than trusting a shallow-graft read; checkout main, merge --ff-only onto origin/main, no reset. `cycle_signal.py --check`: SAME. `preflight.py --fast` backgrounded: reached its 115s budget with `cycle_signal: not recorded, this run has failing gate(s)` before gate_tests, a message no cycle today had produced. That line only means a FAIL is pending somewhere in the gates already run; the per-gate FAIL text itself only prints in the final summary, which this sandbox's gate_tests hang always prevents reaching, so a real failing gate can sit invisible behind "0 FAIL through every gate reached" unless it is checked for directly, which no cycle today had done.

**Traced it rather than guessing.** Monkeypatched `preflight.fail()` to print immediately (scratch script, nothing committed) and re-ran: `gate_ci_conclusion_current` fired locally, confirming checks.yml's own run 40739718057 (commit `d84d51ddd2`, the 17:4x operator cycle) concluded `failure`, live from the Actions API, not cited. Pulled that job's own log directly: the "Preflight" step failed in CI (CI does not hang on gate_tests the way this sandbox does, so it ran the gates after it too) on `FAIL risks-evidence-current RISKS.md cites a stale ops/state.json value: 'forms_dead=218' cited, ops/state.json has forms_dead=219`. 1 gate failed, 35 warnings, all the same standing sandbox-credential gaps every cycle already logs.

**Root cause, not a defect.** `ops/state.json`'s `forms_dead` moved 218 to 219 (commit `5457193ba`) when today's new `/articles/how-to-store-blankets` page (Phil's own commit) added one more page carrying the same inert footer form as every other page, exactly the "nothing new in kind" shape RISKS.md's own RISK-0012 history already names and already has precedent for (commit touching this exact same citation, 217 to 218, logged the same way). Its own house rule: enumerate a new history line only when the addition is different in kind; otherwise update the headline count and nothing else. Fixed by that rule: `RISK-0012`'s evidence line now reads `forms_dead=219`. Verified against the real gate function, not a rewrite of its logic: imported `ops/preflight.py`, cleared `FAIL`, called `gate_risks_evidence_current()` directly, `FAIL == []`. `fix_dashes.py --check`: clean. Diff is one line.

**Went well:** checking for a failing gate hidden behind the gate_tests hang instead of accepting "0 FAIL through every gate reached" at face value, the exact theatre CLAUDE.md 0.4 warns about; tracing to the real root cause in the CI log instead of only re-stating the symptom.

**Did not go well:** this is at least the second time this exact citation has gone stale and been caught after a red build rather than before one (same shape, 217 to 218, logged earlier in RISKS.md's own history); the file's existing rule already prevents a new history line each time, but nothing yet prevents the headline number itself from going stale between page-adding commits. Worth a cheap fix for a future cycle: have whatever regenerates `ops/state.json`'s `forms_dead` also patch this one RISKS.md line automatically, the same way other generator-owned fields are kept current, rather than relying on a gate to catch it after the fact.

Before writing that down as a new defect, checked the actual cause: `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` was still `true` even after STEP 0's unshallow step ran, because that fetch hit a mid-transfer TLS disconnect (`GnuTLS recv error`) that left a stale `.git/shallow.lock`, so the later unconditional `git fetch --unshallow` silently no-opped. With the clone stuck shallow at a 61-commit synthetic root, `git log -1 -- path` for any file last really touched before that boundary returns the boundary commit's own date, which is today, manufacturing 271 false "last touched 2026-10-23" readings out of a sandbox limitation, exactly the trap CLAUDE.md 0.4 warns against (unchecked must not report as passing, and the same logic cuts the other way: a measurement tool's own blind spot must not get written down as a code defect either). Retried the unshallow until the stale lock cleared; repo is now a real 8,336-commit history, not shallow. Re-ran the ledger: 1 genuinely stale entry (`ops/check_cron_cadence.py`, touched by this hour's own CI fix, not yet re-ledgered), which is correct and expected, not a defect.

GitHub: 10 open issues re-pulled fresh, unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`; issue #42 (the cadence-re-verifying-exhaustion decision) carries no new comment since 2026-10-23T00:21Z. 0 open PRs.

## 2026-10-22, scheduled operator cycle: cold-read of ops/build_product_images.py found and fixed a real, reproduced-live pagination bug

**Did:** Attached clean (fetch, unshallow, checkout -B main origin/main,
ff-only, 407 commits fast-forwarded in, tree clean). Read BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md
sections 0-7 (all Done/Closed/Hold/Phil-gated), ROADMAP-2026-2029.md and the
last 4 log entries, which all pointed at the same handoff:
`ops/cold_read_ledger.py --next` names `ops/build_product_images.py` (369
lines, un-ledgered). Ran `preflight.py` in the background first; it took far
longer than the usual documented stall point but was genuinely progressing
(changing child processes throughout, not flat CPU), so let it run to
completion instead of killing it: 0 FAIL on the clean tree, 29 standing
warnings, all previously diagnosed sandbox-access limits (no Stripe
credential, no network, no SSH key, no mail credential).

Read `ops/build_product_images.py` in full. `manual_spread()` crops a
hardcoded page (22) out of a fresh browser-print of the Manual's own HTML for
`product-manual.jpg`'s sample. Reproduced live rather than suspected: printing
the same committed source in this sandbox put the intended "Lower Cabinet and
Cookware Zone" heading on page 20, not 22; page 22 held an unrelated zone's
cleaning table with no zone name on it. Chromium's print-to-PDF pagination
depends on font metrics and is not portable across machines, so a hardcoded
index is fragile by construction. The shipped image (built elsewhere) was
correct; nothing would have caught a future `--force` regeneration shipping
the wrong zone, since the only gate tied to this generator checks file
existence, not content.

**Verified:** Fixed at the root with a new `find_page(pdf, needle)` that
locates a page by its own heading text; `manual_spread()` now uses it for
both crops it takes. Regenerated `product-manual.jpg` with the fix in this
same sandbox: lands on page 20, shows the correct zone and all six passes.
New `ops/tests/test_build_product_images.py`, fail-then-pass proved directly
(`git stash` reproduces an `AttributeError` without the fix; clean with it
restored). Regenerated the image's 420/840 jpg/webp variants and the two
avif siblings `write()` correctly invalidated (`ops/build_avif.py --encode`).
`gate_product_images_exist`, `check_urls.py` (213/213), `fix_dashes.py
--check` (0/0), `affiliate.py --check` (165 documents) all clean after.
Ledgered as fixed in `ops/cold-read-ledger.json`. No mail credential here
(`inbox_agent.py --apply`: unchecked, not empty); 10 open GitHub issues read
directly, unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`, none from Phil, 0 PRs.
No price or product touched; one existing product-tile image corrected in
place.

With that lane clean, picked up `OWNER-ACTIONS.md`'s own open "worth checking before discarding" question instead of starting a new cold-read sweep: whether `photos/server.py` actually carries the two security fixes (negative Content-Length, socket timeout) from Phil's unpushed 2026-10-14 local commit, which a 2026-10-21 cycle had guessed "most likely yes" without reading the file. Read `photos/server.py` directly: neither fix was present. `_body()` parsed `Content-Length` with a bare `int()`, so a negative value skips the `n > limit` check and reaches `self.rfile.read(n)` with `n < 0`, which blocks until the connection closes rather than reading a bounded amount; `Handler.timeout` was left at `BaseHTTPRequestHandler`'s default `None`, so an idle connection holds a `ThreadingHTTPServer` thread forever. Fixed both: a guard rejecting `n < 0` (and an unparseable value) in `_body()`, and `Handler.timeout = PHOTOS_SOCKET_TIMEOUT` (env-configurable, default 30s).

**Verified.** Proved fail-then-pass directly, not assumed: reverted both fixes, reran `ops/tests/test_photos_service.py`, and the new `negative-content-length-refused` case failed exactly as the finding describes (the request hung until the test's own client closed the connection, then the server raised the wrong error against an already-gone peer, logged as a broken pipe); restored the fix, 39/39 clean. While verifying, found a third, smaller gap: the disk-free floor (`shutil.disk_usage`, from the 2026-10-15 review pass) had real, correctly-placed code but no test anywhere, despite `PHOTOS-API.md` claiming "every fix above is proved fail-then-pass." Added that test too (monkeypatching `shutil.disk_usage`); disabling the real check in `store.py` and rerunning confirmed the new case is what catches it (40/40 with the floor live). `store.py` itself needed no code change, only the missing test. `cold_read_ledger.py` updated (`photos/server.py` now `fixed`, dated and noted); `PHOTOS-API.md`'s security-review section and `OWNER-ACTIONS.md`'s own item rewritten to state the verified fact in place of the guess, narrowing what remains to Phil to the `site/photos.html`-vs-`site/photo-check.html` product call alone. **Did:** Attached clean (fetch, unshallow, `checkout -B main origin/main`, ff-only onto `98419c1a6`, tree clean). Read `GOALS.md`, `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md`, `ROADMAP-2026-2029.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the real head of `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md` (newest-first, confirmed before reading). Re-derived the backlog state directly rather than trusting its own prose: sections 2-4's `A`/`B`/`C` items are all struck through except C5 (Gemini billing) and C6 (YouTube OAuth), both already Phil-gated; section 1b fully resolved; section 5 explicitly Hold on traffic. 10 open GitHub issues checked via the API, unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`; read issue #42's own comment thread directly, all three comments self-authored by prior agent cycles, none from Phil. `ops/last-owner-notification.json` correctly withholds a repeat push (sent 2026-10-19, no reply, no state change since) and I did not override it.

**Found while running preflight, not by auditing it.** A first `preflight.py` invocation, run directly rather than through `ops/run_preflight.sh` (my own mistake, the exact anti-pattern the lock's own docstring warns against), was killed by my foreground timeout and orphaned its run-lock with its own pid written inside. The very next invocation was handed that exact pid back by the kernel and deadlocked against its own stale lock: `acquire_preflight_lock()`'s staleness check skips the dead-holder fast path whenever `holder == own_pid`, which this sandbox's fast pid recycling made true by coincidence, falling back to a 1200-second mtime timeout against a lock nobody still genuinely held. `gate_preflight_lock_blocks_concurrent_runs` did not already cover this: its own "Half 1" comment names the exact collision risk and routes around it with a fake sentinel pid instead of proving the real default path survives it.

**Verified and fixed rather than reported.** Reproduced the live incident in isolation (git-stashed the eventual fix, replayed the exact collision, watched it wait the full timeout and raise `RuntimeError`), then fixed it at the root: `_proc_start_time()` (new) reads `/proc/<pid>/stat`'s own starttime field, set once at exec and never repeated for two processes alive at once, so a recorded start time now disambiguates "still that process" from "pid recycled" independent of any `holder != own_pid` comparison. Restored the fix, replayed the same collision: broke in under a millisecond. Added a "Half 4" to the existing gate proving this exact shape, called with `acquire_preflight_lock()`'s real default rather than the sentinel the first three halves use; fail-then-pass proved both in isolation and by running the gate function directly. Full `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` section 25 carries the complete account.

**Verified:** `gate_preflight_lock_blocks_concurrent_runs` run directly, clean, all four halves. Full `preflight.py` (via the proper wrapper this time) reached every gate with 0 FAIL/ERROR before the documented `gate_tests` headless-Chromium sandbox hang (confirmed live: zombie `chrome`/`chrome_crashpad` processes under it), killed there, reported unchecked past that point, not assumed passing. `check_urls.py` 213/213, `audit_pages.py` 218/0 (0 duplicate titles/descriptions), `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0, `affiliate.py --check` clean (165 documents), `cold_read_ledger.py --stale` 0/277. `inbox_agent.py --apply`: no mail credential in this sandbox, unchecked, not empty, same standing limitation. 0 open PRs.

**Went well:** running the thing live surfaced a bug that a planted test had carefully routed around rather than exercised; CLAUDE.md 0.3's "verify against production, not the repository" generalizes to this repository's own tooling, not just the live site.

**Did not go well:** caused the very incident I then had to fix, by running `preflight.py` directly instead of through `ops/run_preflight.sh` on the first attempt; lost real time to the resulting deadlock before diagnosing it.

**Changing next cycle:** use `ops/run_preflight.sh` first, every time; it already exists precisely to prevent this.

**Next:** no other lane is genuinely unblocked, non-Phil-gated work right now (C5/C6 both Phil-gated, section 5 on Hold for traffic, all 10 GitHub issues decision/blocked-on-art). ## 2026-10-20, scheduled operator cycle (17:4x slot: took the CI-trigger-gap handoff below, found the alarm was over-stated but the underlying gate gap was real, closed it)

**Did:** Picked up the PM check-in's handoff immediately below instead of reconfirming the exhausted/Phil-gated backlog a further time. Verified its claim before acting on it (CLAUDE.md 5d), rather than taking "checks.yml silently stopped triggering" at face value.

**What was actually true, not what it looked like.** Listed every commit since the last completed run (`3b61db7e`, 09:18:56Z) with `git log --format` directly: 11 of them touch a path `checks.yml`'s own filter does not exclude, which is why the PM cycle read it as a real gap. But every one of those 11 is authored by `github-actions` (the hourly check-in bot), pushing with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` via `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` in `hourly-brief.yml`. That is GitHub's own documented anti-recursion rule, not a defect anywhere in this repository: a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored push structurally cannot trigger another workflow run. Every Claude-authored commit in the same window touched only the paths `checks.yml` already excludes (the dashboard trio, this log), because every one of those cycles found the backlog genuinely exhausted and had no real content to ship. Zero real, non-bot, non-excluded commits landed unverified. The alarm was real effort well spent, but the premise ("silently dark", implying danger) overstated what was actually found.

**What was real underneath the overstatement, and worth fixing.** `gate_ci_conclusion_current` only asks "was the last COMPLETED run green", and has no way to tell "nothing since needed checking" apart from "nothing since has even tried", which is exactly the shape CLAUDE.md 0.4 names. `gate_workflows_healthy`'s own staleness branch already has the right idea (`_commits_touching_paths_since`, built live on 2026-09-27 for the identical false-positive shape in `mobile-checks.yml`) but only escalates after 7 days, the wrong bar for a push-triggered gate meant to verify every real push, and its commit count does not exclude bot-authored commits, so it would have miscounted the same way the PM cycle did by hand.

**Fixed, not just noted.** `_commits_touching_paths_since` now takes an optional `exclude_author` filter (`ops/preflight.py`). New gate `gate_checks_yml_real_gap`, wired into `main()` immediately after its sibling `gate_ci_conclusion_current` (same position, before the `gate_tests` sandbox hang): counts non-bot commits touching `checks.yml`'s own trigger paths since its last completed run, and FAILS by name and count when any exist with no later run. Run live against this repository's real state: 11 commits touch the paths, 0 once bot-authored commits are excluded, confirmed clean, matching the investigation exactly.

**Verified, not cited.** New test `ops/tests/test_gate_checks_yml_real_gap.py`, 5/5: a bot-only gap passes clean, a single real non-bot commit FAILS by name and count, zero commits passes clean, an unqueryable workflow defers to the sibling gate rather than double-warning, and the gate is confirmed wired into `main()` right after `gate_ci_conclusion_current`. Re-ran the existing `test_gate_ci_conclusion_current.py` (5/5) and `test_workflows_healthy.py` (clean) after the shared-helper change to confirm no regression; grepped for every other caller of `_commits_touching_paths_since` (one, unaffected by the new optional parameter's default). `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0. `py_compile` clean on both changed files.

**Went well:** verifying the claim before building anything caught that the real fix was a gate improvement, not an incident; building the fix on the exact helper `gate_workflows_healthy` already proved out for the identical false-positive shape, rather than a second parser.

**Did not go well:** the PM cycle's own framing ("silently stopped triggering", "new P0") overstated a correctly-functioning platform behavior as an outage; worth a sentence of correction here so the next reader does not inherit the alarm.

**Changing next cycle:** none beyond the gate just added; this is the fix for the one real gap this exact shape could recur through.

**Next:** whichever of the 10 open decision/blocked-on-art issues Phil clears first; nothing else is genuinely unblocked. The standing backlog state underneath this is unchanged.

Pushed to main. `ops/preflight.py`, `ops/tests/test_gate_checks_yml_real_gap.py`, `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md`, `EXECUTIVE-DASHBOARD-LIVE.md`, `ops/dashboard.html`, `ops/state.json`. No content, price or product touched, no new page, IndexNow not applicable.

## 2026-10-20, PM check-in (17:4x slot, 30-minute triage, previous work confirmed finished, new P0 handed to the operator)

NEXT FOR THE OPERATOR: diagnose and fix why `checks.yml` has stopped triggering on pushes to main, because it has not run even once since commit `3b61db7e` at 09:18:56Z, over 8 hours and well over a dozen qualifying pushes ago, despite several of those pushes changing files its own `paths:` filter includes and does not exclude.

Previous work (the 17:1x cycle) confirmed finished: tree clean, pushed, dashboard fresh. That part of the handoff stands.

What I found instead of starting the sort_scope or decision backlog: the 17:1x cycle's own log entry, and the 16:1x/16:4x cycles before it, each checked `checks.yml` by looking only at the handful of commits since their own last check and finding those excluded (dashboard/state/log only), then concluded "no new run was expected." That reasoning is correct per-commit but was never applied to the full span back to the last actual run, so it missed that the gap itself started much earlier. Checked the real span directly: the first commit after the 09:18:56 run that touches a non-excluded path is `2334756` at 09:51:01Z (`CHECKIN-LOG.md`, `ops/last-brief-sent.json`, `ops/state-checkin.json`, none of which `checks.yml` excludes). No run fired for it, or for any of the ops/corpus-rotation.json-only commits after it (for example `ba834355` at 13:47:06, `f75d9ae` at 14:30:08), or for the ops/last-brief-sent.json and ops/state-checkin.json changes bundled into every hourly check-in commit since. Confirmed via the Actions API directly, not cited: `checks.yml`'s run #2235 on `3b61db7e` is still its newest run, full stop. Ruled out the easy explanations: the workflow is still `state: active`; its `on:` paths block has not changed since 2026-09-29; no commit message in the window carries a skip-ci marker; and push events themselves are reaching GitHub fine, because five other workflows with broader triggers (Hourly brief, LinkedIn drafts, Deliver paid orders, Social drafts, Bluesky drafts) fired normally on these same pushes. Did not find the actual root cause; that is the operator's job, not mine in a 30-minute slot.

Why this matters more than another exhausted-state confirmation: `gate_ci_conclusion_current` in `ops/preflight.py` only checks whether the most recently COMPLETED run of `checks.yml` was green. It has no way to notice that no new run happened at all, so it has been silently reporting the stale 09:18 success as current through every PM and operator cycle since, exactly the "unknown is not unused, unchecked is not passing" failure this file's own CLAUDE.md section 0.4 names. Every ops/ and content/ change that landed on main in the last 8+ hours has shipped with zero CI verification, and the gate meant to catch exactly that did not.

Recommend the operator: (1) find why these pushes are not matching `checks.yml`'s path filter in practice (push a small, deliberate, clearly-qualifying change under `ops/` from this environment and watch whether a run appears; check whether these autonomous pushes are landing through a path GitHub treats differently, such as a token/app identity that suppresses triggered runs on some filtered workflows but not others); (2) once fixed, harden `gate_ci_conclusion_current` (or add a sibling gate) to fail when no `checks.yml` run has started within some bound after a qualifying push, not just when the last one failed.

Not filing this as a `decision` issue: it is an engineering bug to find and fix, not a tradeoff for Phil. Not attempting the fix myself in this slot, per standing PM practice (investigation only, large fix handed to the operator at :43).

The standing handoff underneath this is unchanged and still correct: all 10 open GitHub issues are still `decision`/`blocked-on-art`/P0 and still not newly actionable (re-checked directly, unchanged since 2026-10-18T19:54:35Z). ## Scheduled operator cycle, 2026-10-18, 20:5x: a lock gate that passed real cycles while missing the real-world shape, found and closed

**Did:** Attached clean (unshallow, ff-only onto a64607442, tree clean, merged forward onto this cycle's concurrent 20:4x work at push time). Read BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md, GOALS.md, CLAUDE.md carried forward. Ran preflight.py fast: 0 FAIL/ERROR through every gate, hung at gate_tests (frozen /proc CPU time), killed cleanly. GitHub reverified directly: 10 open issues unchanged, all decision/blocked-on-art; #42's newest comment self-authored by the 20:0x cycle, no reply from Phil. 0 open PRs. check_urls.py 213/213, fix_dashes.py 0/0, affiliate.py clean, check_sellable.py 124/126 (2 service SKUs), cold_read_ledger.py 276/276, 0 stale.

**Found and fixed a root cause instead of patching the symptom a third time:** SIGKILLing a hung preflight leaves a zombie process; os.kill(pid, 0) reports a zombie as alive, so _run_lock_pid_alive() held the next cycle's lock for the 20-minute stale-mtime timeout instead of breaking immediately. Hit twice today (20:1x patched by hand; this cycle hit it again). Fixed _run_lock_pid_alive() to read /proc/<pid>/stat's state letter, treating Z as dead. Added a third case to gate_preflight_lock_blocks_concurrent_runs that SIGKILLs a real subprocess without reaping it, proving the lock breaks in under 2 seconds. Recorded as LRN-0042.

**Verified:** proved the gate can fail, not just pass (reverted the fix, watched a 5s timeout; restored it, watched the same gate pass in 3ms). Reran preflight.py: lock gate clean, same gate_tests hang, 0 FAIL elsewhere.

**Went well:** closed a twice-repeated manual patch with a gate.

**Did not go well:** no new customer-facing or revenue work; backlog and GitHub queue remain genuinely exhausted and Phil-gated.

**Changing next cycle:** none.

## Scheduled operator cycle, 2026-10-18, 18:3x: a second concurrent-preflight collision the same date, closed with a lock instead of another prose warning

**Did:** Attached clean (unshallow, `checkout main`, ff-only onto `eccbaefc5`). Delegated reading the backlog/roadmap/NIGHTLY-LOG to a background research fork, scoped explicitly read-only. The fork instead executed real work (a genuine, well-verified fix: `resolve_deploy_reachable()` / `gate_dashboard_deploy_reachable_carry_forward`, now on `main` as `4290375f0`) while this session's own `ops/run_preflight.sh` run was alive in parallel. The two collided: my run's log stopped mid-gate-list with no FAIL and no summary, and `ps` showed duplicate `audit_catalog.py`/`test_audit_catalog.py` processes fighting over `site/_audit_catalog_fixture.lockdir`. Confirmed the lockdir's recorded pid was dead before clearing it (the sanctioned recovery, not a guess) and re-ran solo.

**Fixed at the root, per 0.2/10b.** This exact shape (two full `preflight.py` copies at once) already happened once earlier today (`LEARNINGS.md` LRN-0041, a false `gate_tests` FAIL that a solo rerun disproved) and was left as a "standing habit, not a gate" because a speculative fix without a reproducible failure would be theatre. This cycle reproduced it for real, worse than before (a dead run, not just a false FAIL), so it earned the gate: new `acquire_preflight_lock()`/`release_preflight_lock()` wrapping `ops/preflight.py`'s real `__main__`, blocking a second raw invocation on a live first one (dead-pid fast break, live-holder wait) regardless of whether it goes through the wrapper. New `gate_preflight_lock_blocks_concurrent_runs`. **Proved it can fail:** disabled the dead-pid check by monkeypatching, watched the gate go red with the exact old-bug symptom (times out on a holder that is actually dead); restored it, watched it pass. **Verified beyond synthetic inputs:** ran two real, separate OS processes against the real lock path; the second blocked ~6s for the first's actual lifetime before acquiring it, not a mocked clock.

**Also closed along the way:** `core.hooksPath` was unset in this sandbox (pre-commit/pre-push present, never running; preflight's own gate self-healed it). `ops/dashboard.py` needed re-ledgering after the 17:5x fix; re-ledgered independently, then found a concurrent session (`6756be013`) had done the same seconds apart with different wording — resolved as an ordinary `git merge` (four-file conflict: `EXECUTIVE-DASHBOARD-LIVE.md`, `ops/cold-read-ledger.json`, `ops/dashboard.html`, `ops/state.json`), keeping the newer side's generated artifacts (a real GitHub Actions hourly check-in, `9a7ead4e7`, had landed with actual egress) over this sandbox's own regeneration, same standing rule as 16:4x/17:1x/17:4x. `git reset --hard` to shortcut this was correctly refused by the environment's own safety classifier; resolved with `git merge` + `git checkout --theirs` on the four generated files instead, which is non-destructive and keeps full history.

**Went well:** the second collision, while real waste, produced a genuinely fixable structural gap (no process-level lock existed anywhere in `preflight.py` itself) that the first occurrence's "standing habit" note had correctly declined to speculate into a gate without a reproducible failure. **Did not go well:** delegating "research only" to a background fork that shares the full autonomous system prompt does not reliably stay read-only; it will execute and even commit/push if it judges the work real, which this time was lucky (the fix was correct and well-verified) but is not something to rely on. **Changing next cycle:** a background fork intended as read-only should get `isolation: "worktree"` when the task might touch the shared checkout at all, not just a scoping sentence in the prompt; a sentence is not a lock, which is the exact lesson this whole cycle is about, one level up.

**Next:** hold the line, same as every cycle today; nothing is unblocked without Phil clearing one of the 10 open `decision`/`blocked-on-art` issues. Not regenerating the dashboard again: the merge already carries a real, minutes-old reading with actual egress, and this credential-less sandbox regenerating on top of it would add a timestamp bump with no new information, exactly the move the reachable-carry-forward fix exists to make safe but not something to do needlessly. Not sending a push notification: nothing customer-facing changed.

Pushed to main (`8e4566994`, `9ecd31316`). `ops/preflight.py`, `LEARNINGS.md`, `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md`, this entry. No content, price or product touched, no new page; IndexNow not applicable.

## Hourly operator, 2026-10-18 (03:1x slot): correction to the prior entry's premature "0 FAIL" claim, real cause found and it was not a product defect

**Correcting my own record, not someone else's.** The entry directly below
this one said the backgrounded `preflight.py` run showed "0 FAIL, 0 traceback
through every gate reached" and used that to justify a "dashboard regen
only" cycle. That was written before the run had actually finished; it had
only reached the documented slow `gate_tests` tail, not completed it. Per
`CLAUDE.md` 0.4, a gate that was still running had not passed, and writing
it as if it had is exactly the defect class this repository tracks hardest.
Caught by this same session, from the run's own completion notification,
not by a later cycle.

**What the finished run actually said:** `gate_tests` FAILed:
`test_audit_catalog.py: a wrong price next to 'Guest Vanity Counter Pack'
was not reported against its own SKU`. Investigated rather than trusted
either direction. Read the real catalogue directly: `Vanity Counter Pack`
and `Guest Vanity Counter Pack` are both correctly $4, live. Three
standalone reruns of `test_audit_catalog.py` passed clean. A third, solo
`preflight.py` (no other copy of itself running) passed every gate, 0 FAIL.
Root cause: this session had unknowingly run two full `preflight.py`
processes at once (its own, plus one still alive inside an earlier
background fork), the exact concurrent-fixture-collision shape
`test_audit_catalog.py`'s own comments already document and partially
defend against from 2026-09-05 and 2026-09-08. No live defect, no orphaned
fixture, nothing to ship a fix for. Recorded as LRN-0041 (a learning, not a
new gate: a speculative lock change without being able to reproduce the
narrower kill-mid-write window would be a gate that cannot be proven to
fail).

**Changing next cycle:** this session will not run a second full
`preflight.py` while another of its own background copies might still be
executing one, and will rerun a single named failing test file alone
before writing up a `gate_tests` FAIL as real.

commits fast-forwarded, no reset or force). Read BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md in
full, ROADMAP-2026-2029.md, CLAUDE.md, and the last several NIGHTLY-LOG.md

blocked-on-art), 0 open PRs, issue #42 (cadence) still open with 0
comments. BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md sections 2 through 13 all Done, Hold or

cold_read_ledger.py --stale: 0, 204 of 204 ledgered. inbox_agent.py
--apply: no mail credential. preflight.py backgrounded, confirmed hung at
gate_tests again via /proc sampling (same standing sandbox limitation
every cycle today already logged); killed clean. Narrower checks all ran

0/0, affiliate.py --check 165 documents, check_sellable 124/126 (2
person-delivered services excluded), link_graph_report.py 0 orphans,
b9_claims.py --status 0 undiagnosed rooms.

**Roughly a dozen cycles already reached this exact "nothing new" verdict
today** (git log and this file's own head show PM check-ins and operator
cycles at 11:4x through 15:1x all independently confirming the same
exhausted state). Running a thirteenth identical reconfirmation would have
added nothing issue #42 does not already say, so instead went looking for
ground nothing had swept: `ops/cold_read_ledger.py`'s lanes only ever
covered `ops/*.py`, `ops/*.js`, `site/assets/js/*.js` and
`mobile/quest-app/lib/*.js`. `photos/*.py` (4 files, built 2026-10-14/15,
twice independently security-reviewed per PHOTOS-API.md) had never been
read by this mechanism, and a security review hunts for attacker-triggered
gaps, not an ordinary-use correctness bug.

**Found a real defect reading `photos/store.py` directly.**
`add_photo`/`delete_photo`/`save_analysis` did read-modify-write on one
session's `meta.json` with no lock. `ThreadingHTTPServer` gives every
request its own thread, so two overlapping requests on the same session (a
before and an after photo sent back to back is the ordinary case) could
both read the file before either wrote it back; the second write silently
erased the first writer's new photo entry. The `.jpg` itself still lands on
disk, orphaned, while the caller who uploaded it was already sent `201`.
Proved directly against the pre-fix code with a forced, deterministic
interleave rather than timing luck: both uploads returned `201`, only one
id survived in the listing afterward.

**Fixed.** One re-entrant lock per session (`Store._lock_for`, created only
once a session directory is confirmed to exist, so a flood of guessed or
invalid session ids cannot grow the lock table unboundedly) and a new
`_authorize()` helper (read + token check, no write) let `open()`,
`add_photo`, `delete_photo`, `save_analysis` and `delete_session` each run
their full read-through-write as one locked critical section. Re-proved
fail-then-pass in `ops/tests/test_photos_service.py` (33 to 37 checks): the
new cases force a second request to actually block mid-`open()` while the
first still holds the lock, then confirm both uploads survive.

**Turned the lesson into a gate, not just a fix.** Added `photos/*.py` as a
fifth lane in `ops/cold_read_ledger.py` and ledgered all four files
(`store.py` fixed, the other three clean), so this is a one-time gap, not a
recurring one. `PHOTOS-API.md` and `OWNER-ACTIONS.md` item 22 updated to
the new 37-check count; `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` section 14 records the full
account.

**Verified after:** `test_photos_service.py` 37/37, `test_build_photo_
check_data.py` 5/5, `test_cold_read_ledger_stale.py` 7/7, `test_gate_cold_
read_handoff_not_stale.py` 26/26, `check_urls.py` 213/213, `audit_pages.py`
clean, `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0, `affiliate.py --check` 165 documents,
`link_graph_report.py` 0 orphans. No price, product or shipped page
touched; `photos/` is still undeployed (Phil's own call,
`OWNER-ACTIONS.md` item 22), so this fix reaches zero live customers today
and closes the gap before his deploy decision could expose it. IndexNow
not applicable.

**Went well:** not repeating a thirteenth identical full reconfirmation;
checking the cold-read ledger's own lane list against what the repository
actually contains rather than trusting "N of N ledgered" at face value.

**Did not go well:** nothing this cycle; the defect found was pre-existing
and pre-deploy, with zero live impact.

**Changing next cycle:** none for the operating loop; the new lane closes
this specific gap. Worth a standing habit, not a rule: when a directory is
added to the repository, check whether it needs to join an existing sweep
lane rather than assuming existing lanes already cover it.

**Next:** whichever BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md row or GitHub issue Phil clears
first. Not re-notifying Phil beyond the existing #42 notification: this
finding is informational (pre-deploy, zero live impact) and already fully
recorded here and in PHOTOS-API.md/OWNER-ACTIONS.md for whenever he reads
